subject: Production latency spike — coordinated bridge & remediation timeline
messages:
From: Sara Murphy <sara.murphy@meditrack.io>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-03T09:02:00Z
Subject: Production latency spike — immediate assistance requested

Team,

We started seeing a sustained latency spike across our inference calls to the r-infer-large model at ~08:57 UTC. P95 token latency has climbed from ~120ms to ~1.2s and overall throughput has dropped ~35%. This is impacting customer-facing workflows for our medication reconciliation feature.

Attached is a small log excerpt showing the spike and a few request IDs for follow-up: meditrack_log_snippet.txt (attached).

Can you please triage and let us know estimated ETA for mitigation? We can be available on a bridge now — please escalate as necessary.

Thanks,
Sara Murphy
Head of Engineering, Meditrack
[sara.murphy@meditrack.io]
[attachment: meditrack_log_snippet.txt (text/plain)]

From: david.kim@redwood.ai
To: Sara Murphy <sara.murphy@meditrack.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-03T09:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — immediate assistance requested

Sara — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I’m standing up a dedicated bridge now and pulling in the runtime and infra leads. 

Immediate plan (next 60 minutes):
- 09:08: bridge open (dial-in + Slack channel) — joining now.
- 09:10: quick health check and traffic snapshot (Karthik + infra).
- 09:20: deploy short-term mitigation (degraded model variant + rate-limited batching) if needed.
- 09:45: assess impact and confirm expected restoration timeline or further rollbacks.

Karthik, Marissa, Steph — please prioritize triage. Sara — can you confirm whether enabling our degraded inference mode (reduces model size, preserves API) is acceptable for 15–30 minutes while we remediate? If yes I’ll proceed and send the exec-facing summary for your stakeholders.

Bridge details: https://meet.redwood.com/bridge/meditrack-20271203 (joining now).

-David
David Kim
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[david.kim@redwood.ai]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: david.kim@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Murphy <sara.murphy@meditrack.io>
Date: 2027-12-03T09:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — immediate assistance requested

On Fri, Dec 3, 2027 at 09:08 AM +0000, david.kim@redwood.ai wrote:
> Sara — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I’m standing up a dedicated bridge now and pulling in the runtime and infra leads.

Quick findings from the bridge triage:
- Root cause hypothesis: a combination of a recent autoscaler tweak and a memory pressure pattern on the p4dedicated pool causing increased kernel thrashing for long-sequence requests.
- Short-term mitigations we can push within ~12 minutes:
  * Enable degraded model variant (r-infer-medium-quant) for Meditrack routes — lowers memory footprint and per-token compute.
  * Reduce max concurrent sequences and enable stricter batching window (100ms) to smooth peaks.
  * Temporarily route overflow to a warm fallback pool in eu-west to shed load (will add ~200ms latency for those requests).

I’m attaching the rollback and mitigation steps we executed in other events: rollback_plan.md (internal runbook). If Sara approves degraded mode + transient routing, we’ll implement and monitor immediately.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Runtime Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.ai]
[attachment: rollback_plan.md (text/markdown)]

From: Sara Murphy <sara.murphy@meditrack.io>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-03T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — immediate assistance requested

Thanks — I’m okay with degraded model + transient routing for now. Prioritize availability over strict latency targets; we’ll communicate the temporary UX impact to our ops team.

Please also provide a short exec-facing note I can share with our VP of Product summarizing impact and expected timeline.

Appreciate the rapid response.

Sara
Sara Murphy
Head of Engineering, Meditrack

From: david.kim@redwood.ai
To: Sara Murphy <sara.murphy@meditrack.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ops@meditrack.io
Date: 2027-12-03T11:00:00Z
Subject: Meditrack — interim executive update and post-incident plan (SEV-2)

Sara / Meditrack leadership,

Summary (what happened):
- At ~08:57 UTC on 2027-12-03 we observed increased p95 token latency and reduced throughput for Meditrack’s inference routes. Initial triage pointed to memory pressure + recent autoscaler behavior in the p4dedicated pool.

Immediate actions taken (what we did):
- 09:08 UTC: Redwood bridge opened and triage team engaged.
- 09:20 UTC: With customer approval, we enabled degraded model variant (r-infer-medium-quant) and tightened batching windows.
- 09:30 UTC: Overflow traffic was routed to a warm fallback pool to protect core requests.

Impact and mitigation outcome (status):
- Availability restored to >98% for user-facing flows within ~25 minutes of the bridge opening. P95 latency improved to ~280–350ms on the degraded variant; throughput recovered to within 90% of baseline.

Next steps and timeline (post-incident):
- By 2027-12-04 EOD: Full RCA draft (runtime + autoscaler telemetry).
- By 2027-12-06: Postmortem review with Meditrack (1-hour review meeting) and proposed remediation plan (autoscaler revert + kernel tuning).
- By 2027-12-13: Targeted follow-up (if agreed) to validate fixes on a canary traffic slice.

We will circulate the RCA and a concise one-page exec summary for your VP ahead of the review. Attached are the bridge notes we recorded: bridge_notes_20271203.pdf.

If you want us to keep your stakeholders on a distribution list for live updates or to join the RCA working session, let me know and we’ll add them.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll own the follow-through and keep you updated.

-David
David Kim
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[david.kim@redwood.ai]
